title: Finite scalar comparison and coherence of lisse realization maps
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme, without separatedness [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] set $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(R/t^n)_X$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and $A_X=B_X[1/t]$, the sheafification of sectionwise localization. Use ordinary module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\mathcal C_X=D^b_c(X,R)$ for the integral constructible category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], $Q_X:\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal R_X=D^b_c(X,E)$ for raw rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and $F_X:D(B_X)\to D(A_X)$ for $K\mapsto A_X\otimes^L_{B_X}K$. Write $J_X(Q_XK)=F_XK$, $J_X(u\otimes a)=aF_X(u)$ for the induced functor. A lisse rational object means an object of the standard heart [def-weil-constructible-heart] pro-etale locally isomorphic to a finite sum of coefficient units [def-real-rational-lisse-heart]. A finite locally free module sheaf means one pro-etale locally isomorphic to $A_X^{\oplus r}$, allowing rank zero and varying finite ranks.

For a finite extension $E\subset E'$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, write $B'_X=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E',X}$ and $A'_X=B'_X[1/t']$, with $t'$ a uniformizer of $\mathcal O_{E'}$. There are natural isomorphisms
$$J_{X,E'}(K\otimes_EE')\xrightarrow{\sim}A'_X\otimes^L_{A_X}J_{X,E}K.$$
On integral representatives they are localization of the inverse of the quotient-cone comparison $\chi_{E'/E,K}$ [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], composed with ordinary derived scalar associators. On rational arrows they use $J(u\otimes a)=aF(u)$. On lisse objects they are ordinary coefficient extension in degree zero, send $e_i\otimes b$ to $be_i$, and have the homology-normalized form of [def-real-lisse-field-normalization]. The coefficient ring square commutes with all residue projections and localization units.

The tensor, unit and pullback comparisons specified by the inverse completion maps and ordinary scalar squares in [lem-tw-lisse-tensor-pullback-realization] and the scalar comparisons just specified obey the naturality, tensor associativity, symmetry, both unit, identity-pullback and composition-pullback diagrams. They obey the identity and tower laws for coefficient extensions and their tensor and pullback compatibility diagrams. On integral representatives the diagrams use the same simultaneous finite quotient maps, and their strict inverse-limit cone maps have zero shifted-product coordinate. On degree-zero lisse modules the associator sends $(e_i\otimes e_j)\otimes e_k$ to $e_i\otimes(e_j\otimes e_k)$, the symmetry sends $e_i\otimes e_j$ to $e_j\otimes e_i$ with sign $+1$, units multiply by $1$, successive pullbacks preserve basis vectors, and successive scalar maps multiply their scalars. All these specifications are compatible with sheaf maps and independent of the chosen local bases.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2, Proposition 6.8.14(1), Remark 6.8.15; agent specification of quotient-diagram coherence and finite scalar comparisons

proof.text: First check the geometric hypotheses used below. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and itself. Finite type includes local finite type and quasi-compactness. Thus the local-Noetherian finite-type lemma and the locally-Noetherian quasi-separatedness lemma make every scheme in the statement Noetherian and qcqs; the finite-type dimension lemma makes it finite dimensional. The prime $\ell$ is invertible since the characteristic is different. For $E\subset E'$, use the compatible same-index finite scalar maps to obtain $b:B_X\to B'_X$. Its residue projections are exactly the specified ones. The analogous maps for $E\subset E'\subset E''$ compose, because each finite quotient map does; joint monicity of inverse-limit projections proves equality of completed ring maps. For a scheme map the constant-section maps commute with coefficient inclusions, so the same projection calculation proves the coefficient ring square, with the geometric inverse-image compositor supplied by completed-coefficient ringed coherence. The valuation restriction assertion puts $t$ in the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{E'}$; the DVR factorization gives $t=u(t')^e$ with $u$ a unit and $e\ge1$. Thus inverting $t$ or $t'$ in $B'_X$ gives the same sheaf, and $b$ induces $a:A_X\to A'_X$. Equality on the integral rings extends uniquely across localization. This proves the residue and localization-unit specifications, including repeated fields.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2 and Remark 6.8.15; agent quotient-cone comparison argument

proof.text:
Write $C_{E'/E}K=B'_X\otimes^L_{B_X}K$ and $I_{E'/E}K$ for the specified integral scalar extension. The finite-free completed scalar comparison gives the natural isomorphism $\chi_K:C_{E'/E}K\to I_{E'/E}K$ on the derived-complete integral input $K$. Define $\sigma_K$ to be $A'_X\otimes^L_{B'_X}\chi_K^{-1}$ followed by the ordinary balanced associators
$$A'_X\otimes^L_{B'_X}(B'_X\otimes^L_{B_X}K)\cong A'_X\otimes^L_{B_X}K\cong A'_X\otimes^L_{A_X}(A_X\otimes^L_{B_X}K).$$
The last isomorphism uses $B_X\to A_X\to A'_X$ from step 1. Change of rings and its K-flat computation give these functors; the normalized ordinary monoidal comparisons give these particular associators. Hence $\sigma$ has exactly the requested source, target and integral normalization. Only the derived morphism $\chi^{-1}$ is used; no chain inverse is chosen.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2 and Remark 6.8.15; agent quotient-cone comparison argument

proof.text: The isomorphism in step 2 is natural on integral arrows since $\chi$ and the balanced associators are natural. In raw rationalization an arrow is a finite sum of $u\otimes c$. Both routes through its naturality square multiply the integral square by the image of $c\in E\subset E'$. The balancing relation $(ru)\otimes c=u\otimes rc$ is respected by $R$-linearity. Additivity proves naturality on all rational arrows with the action $J(u\otimes c)=cF(u)$. Integral inverses remain inverses after localization. This constructs the asserted natural isomorphism on the raw rational categories without any extra objects.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2 and Remark 6.8.15; agent quotient-cone comparison argument

proof.text: The completed integral finite-free lemma identifies $B'_X$, as a $B_X$-module, with a finite product of copies of $B_X$. By step 1, $A'_X=B'_X[1/t]$, so the same finite basis identifies $A'_X$ over $A_X$ with a finite direct sum of copies of $A_X$. Tensoring with it is a finite direct sum functor, hence is exact on module sheaves and has no higher derived terms. Slice restriction and exact localization identify a lisse input locally with $A_X^{\oplus r}[0]$. On the integral coefficient unit the quotient comparison is the actual quotient augmentation; its inverse followed by localization sends a scalar to that same scalar. Additivity gives $\sigma$ on each local free sum: under the canonical scalar-extension identification it sends $e_i\otimes b$ to $be_i$. Its degree-zero identification is the one inducing the identity on $\mathcal H^0$. These are precisely the requirements of the field normalization definition, rather than a new choice of normalization.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2 and Remark 6.8.15; agent quotient-cone comparison argument

proof.text: First retain the ordinary, uncompleted operations. Apply the ringed derived monoidal comparison theorem to completed and localized coefficient rings and their commuting structural squares from step 1. It gives associativity, signed symmetry, both unit equations, and the monoidal identity and composition comparators for ordinary pullback. The finite-derived normalization theorem identifies these maps on simultaneous flat-term K-flat representatives: $s\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(s\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$, with inverse multiplying the two scalar factors. It also gives the scalar-square equation and its identity and successive-change laws. These apply to arbitrary commutative ring-sheaf maps; no flatness of a finite residue coefficient map is being used.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2 and Remark 6.8.15; agent quotient-cone comparison argument

proof.text: Compare those ordinary equations with the actual completed tensor and pullback maps. Use simultaneous flat-term K-flat representatives of the integral inputs and their strict quotient towers. Coherent substitution identifies each iterated completed expression with the limit of its whole finite tensor/pullback expression, including the structural associators, symmetry, unitors and pullback compositors. The quotient-realization theorem says that the finite comparison diagrams commute as strict systems and realize the specified completed maps. For the augmentations from ordinary expressions, project to level $n$: both routes reduce the same tensor generators and apply the finite maps of step 5. For example reassociation sends $((x\otimes y)\otimes z)$ to $x\otimes(y\otimes z)$ after the same coefficient projection; symmetry contributes $(-1)^{pq}$ on degrees $p,q$ on both routes. Unit maps multiply by the projected $1$. The unshifted product maps therefore agree. Their shifted-product coordinates are both zero by the quotient augmentation normalizations. Equality of these two coordinates proves equality of the chain maps to the specified cone, before localization. The cited simultaneous substitution and representative independence make this an equality of the required derived maps, not an inference from isolated finite cohomology groups.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2 and Remark 6.8.15; agent quotient-cone comparison argument

proof.text: On integral constructible inputs the tensor and pullback augmentations used in step 6 are isomorphisms. The tensor/pullback realization lemma specifies its comparisons by precisely their inverses and the ordinary scalar squares. Consequently inserting those inverses into the commuting augmentation diagrams of step 6 cancels each augmentation with its inverse and yields the requested tensor associativity, symmetry and both unit diagrams. The same cancellation applied to the finite identity and composable-pullback systems yields identity-pullback and composition-pullback diagrams; their completed compositors are the specified ones by coherent substitution. Apply exact scalar localization to these equalities and then the scalar-linear arrow argument of step 3. This gives naturality and the same equations on rational objects, for arbitrary scheme morphisms, without separatedness or base-field linearity.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2 and Remark 6.8.15; agent quotient-cone comparison argument

proof.text:
For $E\subset E'\subset E''$, apply the scalar-completion associator normalization. Writing $C$ for ordinary and $I$ for completed scalar extension, it states
$$a^I I_{E''/E'}(\chi_{E'/E})\chi_{E''/E',C_{E'/E}K}=\chi_{E''/E,K}a^C.$$
The input $K$ is derived complete, as required; ordinary finite scalar extension is complete by the finite-free comparison. Invert the displayed isomorphisms and apply $A''_X\otimes^L_{B''_X}(-)$. Substitute the definition of $\sigma$ from step 2: the intermediate $\chi$ factors cancel, leaving exactly the scalar tower equation with the ordinary rational associator. The identity normalization of the finite-free comparison gives the identity field law under multiplication and completeness unitors, including repeated fields. The associator lemma also supplies independence of cofinal exponent choices and the pentagon, so this calculation uses the prescribed strict quotient towers even for ramified extensions.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2 and Remark 6.8.15; agent quotient-cone comparison argument

proof.text: For tensor/scalar and pullback/scalar compatibility, use the mixed coefficient equation of the quotient-realization theorem, together with the ordinary coefficient square of the finite-derived normalization theorem. At level $n$ its scalar association is $(x\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes ab$. The tensor/pullback square has both routes $b\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$; for a single pulled-back generator both routes retain that generator and its image scalar. Thus the actual quotient transitions agree, including the ramified case. The whole-system equation in that theorem identifies the completed structural maps with these same strict maps; the scalar-completion associator of step 8 fixes successive scalar substitutions. The augmentations have the specified zero shifted coordinate. After passing to derived maps, invert the completion isomorphisms and cancel adjacent factors as in step 7. Ordinary associativity identifies the surviving maps with $\sigma$ and the stated tensor/pullback realizations. This proves their mixed diagrams and their identity and tower compatibility. Rational arrows are handled by multiplying scalars as in step 3.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2 and Remark 6.8.15; agent quotient-cone comparison argument

proof.text: Finally restrict to a common pro-etale cover trivializing the finitely many lisse inputs. Slice compatibility of localization and the tensor/pullback realization formulas identify all maps just constructed with ordinary degree-zero module maps. The formulas in steps 4 and 5 send $(e_i\otimes e_j)\otimes e_k$ to $e_i\otimes(e_j\otimes e_k)$, interchange $e_i,e_j$ with sign $(-1)^{0\cdot0}=1$, and multiply unit coefficients by $1$. Consecutive pullbacks retain the same basis vector; consecutive scalar extensions send $(e_i\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $e_i\otimes bc$. These formulas also cover rank zero (the unique map of zero modules) and independently varying finite ranks. For a sheaf map represented on an overlap by a matrix $(m_{ji})$, either composite sends $e_i$ to $\sum_j a(m_{ji})e_j$, with the same scalar image $a$; tensor products give products of matrix entries. In particular the formulas commute with each change-of-basis matrix and its inverse. Hence they are independent of bases and agree on overlaps, so sheaf locality gives the claimed global compatibility with sheaf maps. No local equality test for arbitrary derived morphisms is used here: these are maps of degree-zero sheaves.
